projects.name: Hugging Face Hub datasets (hf:// in DuckDB)
projects.what: Hosted git-like dataset repositories that DuckDB reads directly through hf:// paths, with glob, private access tokens and revisions.
projects.overlap: Authenticated remote query, glob over partitions, versioned snapshots; a hosted alternative to the Linux box for the data plane.
projects.takeaways: Verified: `hf://datasets/user/dataset/path`, glob patterns work (`.../*.parquet`), private or gated access with `CREATE SECRET (TYPE huggingface, TOKEN '...')` or the credential_chain provider that reads ~/.cache/huggingface/token, revisions with `user/dataset@branch`. This is the user experience that Adele should match: one URL scheme, one secret, glob, revision pinning. Using HF itself would give auth + query + sync (the `hf` CLI downloads incrementally, from memory, not verified) with zero server code, but it is a third-party host, refresh every 15 min as git commits is awkward, and it conflicts with the self-hosted goal.
projects.status: Core DuckDB feature, documented for 2.0 (verified). HF pricing and limits for private datasets not checked.

projects.name: ROAPI
projects.what: Rust server (DataFusion) that exposes static files as read-only APIs: SQL, GraphQL, REST, Flight SQL and Postgres wire protocol.
projects.overlap: Read-only HTTP SQL over Parquet, CSV and xlsx with no code.
projects.takeaways: Verified: Apache-2.0; reads CSV, JSON, Parquet, xls/xlsx/ods, Delta; tables can be registered at runtime by POST to /api/table. The "authentication layer" is only an item in a feature list, with no description, so keys would again be checked in a proxy. The SQL dialect is DataFusion, not DuckDB, which breaks the spec (`query "<duckdb sql>"` identical on server and on local pull). Partition handling and reload are not documented on the README.
projects.status: Apache-2.0. A metadata index lists release v0.12.6; date and recent activity not verified.

projects.name: Datasette + datasette-parquet
projects.what: Datasette plugin that serves a DuckDB file or a directory of Parquet/CSV/JSONL files through Datasette's web UI and JSON API.
projects.overlap: Read-only HTTP SQL and browsing over Parquet.
projects.takeaways: Verified: Apache-2.0; files with a common name become one union view; `watch: true` picks up new files; read-only. Limits stated by the author: queries are transpiled from SQLite syntax with sqlglot (so the agent would not write real DuckDB SQL), no query timeout, long queries cannot be interrupted, facets partly disabled, "think carefully" before anonymous exposure. Changelog reaches 0.4 only. One idea to keep from Datasette in general: metadata (descriptions, units) served next to the data from the same endpoint.
projects.status: Apache-2.0, 55 commits, releases up to 0.4; last commit date and Datasette 1.0 compatibility not verified. Looks dormant.

projects.name: Seafowl (Splitgraph / EDB)
projects.what: Single-binary analytical database on DataFusion with an HTTP SQL API designed for CDN caching; stores Parquet with the Delta protocol.
projects.overlap: HTTP SQL endpoint with cache semantics.
projects.takeaways: Verified: Apache-2.0; queries POSTed to /q; the API "follows HTTP cache semantics" so results can be cached by Varnish or a CDN; write access is controlled by a setting, read auth is not described. DataFusion dialect, not DuckDB. Idea to keep for Adele's HTTP fallback: GET with the query in the URL plus an ETag derived from the dataset version, so that repeated agent queries between two refreshes cost nothing.
projects.status: Apache-2.0. Not marked archived on the page; a third-party index gives the last push as 2025-02-25; Splitgraph was acquired by EDB in 2023 (third-party source). Treat as unmaintained, not verified.

projects.name: Iceberg REST catalogs (Lakekeeper, Polaris) with DuckDB
projects.what: Standard REST catalog for Iceberg tables; DuckDB attaches to it with an iceberg secret (OAuth2).
projects.overlap: Catalog, snapshots (knowledge time), authenticated access.
projects.takeaways: From DuckDB docs as returned by search (pages not read in full): DuckDB reads REST catalogs only on S3, S3 Tables and GCS storage, with no local filesystem backend, and a Lakekeeper recipe with an OAuth2 secret exists. For one Linux box this means: a catalog service + its Postgres + an S3 server (MinIO or Garage) + an identity provider. That is four services for a dozen tables. DuckLake gives the same snapshots with one file. Only relevant if non-DuckDB engines (Spark, Trino) must read the data.
projects.status: Not verified in depth; Lakekeeper and Polaris repos not opened. One July 2026 user report of 403 errors with Lakekeeper credential vending to DuckDB (single source, unverified).

projects.name: Pooch
projects.what: Python library that downloads data files only when needed into a local cache, driven by a registry of file names and hashes.
projects.overlap: `adele pull` in the Python client: a registry with hashes, a local cache, an HTTP downloader.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the landing page: v1.9.0 documented, registry files, hash guides, an Authentication guide and an `HTTPDownloader` class exist (contents of these guides not read). The pattern is the right one for pull: the server publishes `partition file --> sha256`, the client downloads a file only if the local hash differs. But the pooch registry is normally shipped inside the package, while Adele's manifest changes every 15 minutes, so writing the diff with httpx or requests (about 100 lines) is simpler than bending pooch. DVC, Quilt, intake and fsspec were on the starting list and were not checked: DVC and Quilt version data with git or S3 (heavy for datasets refreshed every 15 min), intake is a catalog of loaders with no sync, fsspec's HTTP filesystem is a possible transport only.
projects.status: v1.9.0 docs dated 2026 (verified); license not shown on the page (BSD-3 from memory). DVC, Quilt, intake, fsspec, Source Cooperative private access, MinIO/Garage: not verified (Source Cooperative's proxy is documented as anonymous read-only for public data and the platform says private beta, from search results only).

results.angle_summary: The heavy catalogs (DataHub, OpenMetadata, Unity Catalog, Gravitino, Marquez) are too heavy to reuse for a dozen datasets (JVM services, Postgres/Elasticsearch/Neo4j), and Amundsen (archived 2026-09-29) and Vanna (archived 2026-03-29) are dead. Their agent interfaces converge on the same small pattern, which transfers: (1) one discovery entry point that narrows progressively, (2) a separate call for time coverage and freshness, (3) token budgets and pagination on schema output, (4) free-text "ai instructions" stored next to the dataset, (5) skills shipped with the server. Closest prior art is Catalyst Cooperative's agent-skills (energy data, Frictionless datapackage.json, Parquet, DuckDB, SKILL.md, no MCP): it validates the Adele design almost point by point. Challenge to the spec: vendors that started with MCP (DataHub, MotherDuck, Malloy, Rill) all added skills afterwards, which supports "skill + CLI first"; but none of them exposes knowledge time or ETA of next refresh, so Adele must design those fields itself.

projects.name: Catalyst Cooperative agent-skills (datapackage + pudl skills)
projects.what: Two agent skills from the maintainers of PUDL (US open energy data): a generic 'datapackage' skill for any Frictionless Data Package, and a 'pudl' skill with the domain knowledge for their Parquet tables published on a public S3 bucket.
projects.overlap: Almost the whole agent-facing side of Adele: Frictionless descriptor as catalog, Parquet + DuckDB, SKILL.md with progressive disclosure, no MCP, energy domain.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the two SKILL.md pages. (1) Split in two skills: a generic one for the descriptor format, a dataset-specific one for domain knowledge; pudl declares the datapackage skill as a required companion in a 'compatibility' frontmatter field. (2) Hard rule 'never load the full descriptor into context': the agent queries datapackage.json selectively with jq. For Adele, 'adele describe <dataset> [--field x]' plays that role, and the output must stay small. (3) Workflow steps: locate descriptor --> query metadata selectively --> surface usage warnings before presenting a resource --> check primaryKey/foreignKeys before joins --> load with pushdown (DuckDB SELECT ... LIMIT, polars scan_parquet). The 'usage warnings shown before loading code' step maps to Adele's status and revision policy. (4) Reference index in SKILL.md: each reference file is listed with 'when to read it'. (5) Descriptor cache with a TTL (copies under one day old are reused; script fetch_descriptor.py). (6) Publishers add custom fields; '_'-prefixed keys mean system-generated: a convention Adele could use to separate authored fields from server-computed ones. (7) Handles both Data Package v1 ('profile') and v2 ('$schema'). The datapackage skill could be installed as is next to an Adele skill.
projects.status: MIT repo, skills licensed CC-BY-4.0; 148 commits; pudl skill metadata says last updated 2026-08-15. Release/last commit date not checked.

projects.name: Malloy Publisher (MCP endpoint + bundled skills)
projects.what: The open-source server for Malloy semantic models. It serves REST plus one MCP endpoint with five tools, and ships agent skills.
projects.overlap: Design of the discovery call (list/describe) and of the skill delivery; HTTP fallback.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the docs page. (1) One discovery tool, malloy_getContext, where every parameter is optional: no argument --> environments; then packages; then sources; then the fields most relevant to a plain-English query. This is progressive disclosure built into a single call; Adele could merge list and describe the same way ('adele describe' with no argument = list). (2) Forgiving behaviour: a parameter given without its parent is ignored and the caller gets the parent list back instead of an error. (3) Values returned by discovery are directly the arguments of the query tool. (4) Skills are shipped by the server: hosts that support skills load the files, hosts that only support MCP get each skill as an MCP prompt. Adele equivalent: 'adele skill install' or an HTTP endpoint that serves the current SKILL.md, so that the skill version matches the server version. (5) A compile-only tool (malloy_compile) that validates without executing: for Adele, a 'query --dry-run' (DuckDB EXPLAIN) is cheap to add.
projects.status: Open source (Malloy is MIT; Publisher license not checked). A search result reports the repo last pushed 2026-04-21; not verified on the repo.

projects.name: Rill (MCP server, ai_instructions, project skills)
projects.what: BI-as-code tool on DuckDB/ClickHouse with a metrics layer in YAML. Its MCP server exposes metrics views, also from local Rill Developer (http://localhost:9009/mcp).
projects.overlap: list / describe / coverage / query tool set; free-text agent instructions in the dataset YAML.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the docs page. Tool set is exactly Adele's shape: list_metrics_views, get_metrics_view (spec with dimensions and measures), query_metrics_view_summary (the available time range), query_metrics_view, plus list_skills / load_skill. (1) Time coverage is a separate, cheap call that the agent is told to make before querying: supports Adele's server-computed coverage and freshness fields, and suggests showing them in 'adele list' already. (2) 'ai_instructions' field at two levels (project rill.yaml and each metrics view YAML), injected automatically; long guidance goes to skills instead. For Adele: an 'adele: agent_notes' text field per dataset in the authored YAML (pitfalls such as DST, sign conventions, revisions). (3) load_skill with an unknown name returns the list of valid names: error messages that teach the agent. Rill itself is a dashboard product, which is a non-goal for Adele.
projects.status: Apache-2.0 per my memory, not checked on this run. Actively developed (Go package versions v0.87-v0.88 appear in search results). Older docs name the time tool query_metrics_view_time_range; current docs name it query_metrics_view_summary.

projects.name: DataHub MCP server + DataHub Skills
projects.what: MCP server for the DataHub metadata platform (search, entities, schema fields, lineage, real queries, aspect history) and an open-source skills registry on top.
projects.overlap: Catalog exposed to agents; schema output sized for a context window; version history of metadata.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the README. DataHub itself is too heavy for Adele (Kafka, Elasticsearch, SQL store). Ideas that transfer: (1) explicit token budgets: TOOL_RESPONSE_TOKEN_LIMIT (default 80,000 per response), ENTITY_SCHEMA_TOKEN_BUDGET (16,000 per entity), field descriptions cut at 120 characters, list_schema_fields paginated with a remainingCount. Adele's describe should have a compact default and a keyword filter on fields for wide tables. (2) get_dataset_queries returns real SQL that references a dataset: Adele could store 2-3 vetted example queries per dataset in the descriptor, which is cheaper and more reliable than letting the agent guess. (3) get_aspect_history returns the current value plus past versions of a metadata aspect: Adele's descriptors in git plus a schema changelog ('adele describe --history') would give the agent the schema drift history. (4) Mutation tools are off unless an env flag is set: read-only by default. (5) DataHub Skills docs (https://docs.datahub.com/docs/dev-guides/agent-context/skills): five skills (setup, search, lineage, enrich, quality), installed with 'npx skills add datahub-project/datahub-skills'; stated rationale 'MCP provides tools, skills provide instructions, you need both'.
projects.status: Apache-2.0. Release date not shown on the page (not checked). Skills registry announced in 2026.

projects.name: dbt MCP server
projects.what: Official MCP server for dbt: discovery of models and sources, semantic layer queries, SQL execution, dbt CLI commands, job administration.
projects.overlap: Freshness and health status exposed to agents; too large a tool surface as a counter-example.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the README. (1) Freshness is a first-class agent fact: get_all_sources returns every source with its freshness status, and get_model_health returns run status, test results and upstream source freshness in one call. Adele's 'status' field should be a similar single health summary (last fetch result, schema check, freshness versus expected refresh). dbt's source freshness model (warn_after / error_after thresholds on a loaded_at column) is a good template for the 'adele: refresh' block. (2) Counter-example: more than 60 tools in 9 groups, with a list of deprecated per-type detail tools replaced by a generic get_node_details. Lesson: one generic describe, not one tool per kind. dbt itself is not useful to Adele (it transforms data inside a warehouse; Adele only fetches and normalizes).
projects.status: Apache-2.0, active (tool list includes recent Fusion/LSP tools). Release date not shown on the page (not checked).

projects.name: MotherDuck agent-skills (and duckdb-skills)
projects.what: Open-source catalog of 17 SKILL.md skills that teach coding agents DuckDB SQL and MotherDuck workflows, published after MotherDuck already had an MCP server.
projects.overlap: The Skill part of Adele, and the DuckDB dialect guidance that 'adele query' needs.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the blog post (https://motherduck.com/blog/motherduck-agent-skills/). (1) Stated reason for skills: with tools alone, agents write PostgreSQL-style SQL against DuckDB; skills carry the judgment (defaults, mistakes to avoid). Adele's SKILL.md needs a short DuckDB dialect section or should point to an existing duckdb-sql skill. (2) Three layers: utility skills (connect, explore, query, duckdb-sql), workflow skills, use-case skills. For a dozen datasets one Adele skill with reference files is enough, but the 'explore before query' order is the same. (3) Only name + description are loaded at start, the body on match: the description line of Adele's skill must list the trigger topics (ENTSO-E, day-ahead prices, bidding zones...), as the pudl skill does. The duckdb-sql skill could be recommended as a companion.
projects.status: MIT. Blog post undated on the page; repo activity not checked. The separate 'duckdb-skills' repo (attach-db, query, read-file) appeared in search results and is referenced by the Catalyst skills; not opened.

projects.name: OpenMetadata MCP server
projects.what: MCP server built into the OpenMetadata catalog (enabled by default): 15 tools for search, entity details, lineage, context documents, data quality, and writes.
projects.overlap: Catalog exposed to agents; authentication per person and per bot.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the docs. Too heavy to reuse (Java server, MySQL/Postgres, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, ingestion on Airflow). Ideas: (1) get_entity_details takes optional includes (context, lineage, quality, content): one describe call with opt-in sections instead of many tools. Maps to 'adele describe --samples --stats --history'. (2) Three auth modes: OAuth for interactive use, personal token with the user's rights, bot JWT for unattended agents. Adele's 'API key per team member' is the personal token; consider a separate key type for scheduled agents so that the logs distinguish them. (3) root_cause_analysis traces a quality failure to its origin: for Adele the equivalent is that the status field says which fetcher failed and since when, in the describe output. (4) Their tool list was consolidated (several per-type tools replaced by generic ones), same lesson as dbt.
projects.status: Apache-2.0 per my memory (not checked on this run). Docs are under a v2.0.x path; the version that introduced MCP was not found.

projects.name: Boring Semantic Layer (BSL)
projects.what: Lightweight semantic layer in Python on Ibis (dimensions and measures as lambdas), inspired by Malloy, with an MCP wrapper class.
projects.overlap: Small-scale, DuckDB-compatible alternative to raw SQL for agents; tool set.
projects.takeaways: README verified: MIT, 809 commits, models defined in Python with Ibis (to_semantic_table, with_measures), works on any Ibis engine including DuckDB, described as 'MCP-friendly'. From secondary sources only (a Substack post by the author and skill listings, not the README): an MCPSemanticModel class based on FastMCP with four tools (list models, get model, get time range, query model), where each tool docstring serves as the prompt; later versions seem to add get_documentation. Again a dedicated time-range tool. For Adele: a semantic layer (measures, joins) adds little for a dozen raw time-series tables where the agent writes DuckDB SQL; the descriptor with grain + units is the right level. Reconsider only if the same derived metrics (spreads, residual load) get recomputed inconsistently.
projects.status: MIT. Release date not shown (not checked). MCP tool names not verified on a primary page.

projects.name: Wren AI (MDL semantic layer, CLI + skills + MCP)
projects.what: Open-source 'GenBI' engine: a semantic and context layer in a git-friendly Modeling Definition Language, exposed to agents through a CLI, installable skills, SDKs and an MCP server.
projects.overlap: CLI + skills as the primary agent interface; units and enums in the model definition.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the README. (1) Product direction matches Adele's choice: 'pip install wrenai', then 'wren query', 'wren ask', and 'wren skills get <workflow>' (the CLI hands out its own skills), plus 'npx skills add Canner/WrenAI'. The old Docker multi-service app is now 'Classic' on a legacy branch with no new features; the engine was merged into this repo on 2026-05-07. So a previously heavy project moved to CLI + skills. (2) MDL covers models, columns, relationships, views, metrics, and context such as enums, units and approved joins: confirms that units and allowed values belong in the field descriptor. DuckDB is a supported connector. Not reusable as a whole: it is aimed at text-to-SQL over a warehouse and has no fetch, freshness or revision concepts.
projects.status: Engine, SDK and skills Apache-2.0; repo also has AGPL-3.0 and CC-BY-4.0 files; security features and the GenBI UI are commercial. Active in 2026. Release version not shown (not checked).

projects.name: DataCharter
projects.what: Small Python tool: a local SQL workspace where DuckDB federates files and databases and a charter.yaml contract governs what agents can see, served over a CLI and an MCP endpoint.
projects.overlap: Closest in size and stack to the Adele server: DuckDB, one YAML contract as the catalog, one binary, read-only agent access, shared HTTP endpoint for a team.
projects.takeaways: Verified on PyPI and the repo page. Workspace is a directory with charter.yaml, queries/ and guides/ (saved queries and prose guidance next to the contract; exact role of each not documented on the pages read). Access is default-deny with 'principals:' and 'grants:'; 'datacharter access diff' shows access changes in a pull request. For Adele, the analogous useful command is a schema diff on a descriptor change in a PR ('adele catalog diff'), which supports 'never changes schema silently'. Its focus is governance (PII masking, audit log, red-team tests), which Adele does not need for public data. No fetchers, no freshness, no time axes. Repo is tagged 'odcs' but the page does not say the contract follows ODCS.
projects.status: Apache-2.0. PyPI 0.44.0 released 2026-09-15, self-described pre-release. 17 stars, 226 commits: single-vendor, very small community.

projects.name: Apache Ossie (incubating), formerly Open Semantic Interchange (OSI)
projects.what: Vendor-neutral YAML specification for semantic models (datasets, fields, relationships, metrics) with an 'ai_context' block of instructions for agents.
projects.overlap: Alternative or complement to the Frictionless descriptor; the 'adele:' extension block.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the project site: Apache-2.0, repo https://github.com/apache/ossie, example file uses version '0.3.0.dev0', top level has version, name, description, ai_context.instructions, then datasets with fields (name, expression.sql, optional dimension.is_time) and metrics. No units on the page read. Assessment for Adele: Frictionless stays the better base because it describes physical tabular data (types, keys, paths) and already has tooling and a skill; Ossie describes metrics and joins, has no coverage, freshness or revision concepts, and is still a moving draft. One idea to copy: name the free-text agent guidance field 'ai_context' with 'instructions' and 'examples', so that it is recognizable. From secondary sources only: renamed and accepted in the Apache Incubator on 2026-07-10; Apache Polaris stores Ossie documents next to tables.
projects.status: Apache-2.0, incubating, spec in draft (0.3.0.dev0 seen on the site). Incubation date and Polaris integration not verified on a primary page.

projects.name: Cube (MCP server)
projects.what: Semantic layer (cubes, views, measures in YAML/JS) with an MCP server of 30 tools on the hosted platform.
projects.overlap: Compact discovery records; refresh status of materialized partitions.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the docs page. The MCP server is a hosted endpoint (cubecloud.dev/mcp) configured in the Admin console; the page does not say that it works with self-hosted Cube Core, so it is not reusable here. Most of the 30 tools are for dashboard authoring, model editing and git branches. Two details worth copying: searchDataModel returns 'compact records (name, title, description, type)' (a short form for list), and runQuery returns schema + one page of rows + hasMore/totalRows (Adele's query should cap rows by default and say how many remain). getPreAggregationStatus (partition counts, build times, build errors) is the nearest thing to a per-partition refresh status.
projects.status: Cube Core is Apache-2.0 per my memory (not checked). MCP availability for the open-source core: not confirmed.

projects.name: Unity Catalog OSS
projects.what: Open-source catalog for tables, volumes, functions and models (LF AI & Data sandbox project), with a REST API and a DuckDB extension.
projects.overlap: Catalog server in front of Parquet/Delta files queried by DuckDB.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the README: Apache-2.0, needs JDK 17 and an sbt build (or Docker Compose / Helm), DuckDB reads it with "ATTACH 'unity' AS unity (TYPE UC_CATALOG)". No MCP interface is described on the page (the repo has an 'ai' directory whose contents I did not open). Too heavy and wrong focus for Adele: it manages namespaces, table locations and permissions, and has no fields for units, grain, freshness or revisions. The only transferable idea is the user experience of one ATTACH statement: 'adele pull' could generate a local DuckDB file with one view per dataset, so that the agent attaches one file.
projects.status: Apache-2.0, LF AI & Data sandbox. Latest release not shown (not checked). MCP support not verified.

projects.name: Apache Gravitino
projects.what: Federated metadata catalog ('metadata lake') over many sources, with Iceberg and Lance REST catalogs, a Trino connector, and an mcp-server directory in the repo.
projects.overlap: Catalog with an MCP server.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the repo: Apache-2.0, Java server started with gravitino.sh or a Docker Compose playground; the mcp-server folder exists and is a Python project managed with uv (pyproject.toml, uv.lock). I could not read which tools it exposes (the docs page returned empty content). Built to federate Hive, Iceberg, Kafka, JDBC catalogs across regions: the opposite of a dozen Parquet datasets on one box. No idea specific enough to transfer.
projects.status: Apache-2.0, Apache top-level project, active. MCP tool list not verified. Latest release not checked.

projects.name: Dead or unsuitable: Amundsen, Vanna, Marquez/OpenLineage, Evidence, Data Contract CLI (ODCS)
projects.what: Group entry for the remaining starting points: Amundsen (catalog), Vanna (text-to-SQL), Marquez (OpenLineage server), Evidence (BI as code), plus Data Contract CLI as an unlisted neighbour.
projects.overlap: Catalog, lineage and run history, contracts with schema checks.
projects.takeaways: Amundsen: repo page says archived by the owner on 2026-09-29 'due to inactivity'; needed Neo4j or Atlas + Elasticsearch + Flask services. Vanna (https://github.com/vanna-ai/vanna): archived 2026-03-29, MIT; it was a text-to-SQL agent framework, not a catalog. Marquez (https://github.com/MarquezProject/marquez): alive (LF AI & Data graduated), Java 17 + PostgreSQL, HTTP and GraphQL APIs, no MCP mentioned; it records datasets, jobs and runs from OpenLineage events. Idea only: Adele's fetchers could write one run record per fetch (start, end, status, rows, schema hash) in a small table, which is what the status, freshness and ETA fields are computed from; emitting OpenLineage events would be over-engineering. Evidence: search results show a docs MCP server and a login-gated Studio MCP on evidence.studio (hosted product); dashboards are a non-goal. Data Contract CLI (https://cli.datacontract.com/, ODCS from the Bitol project): search results say it lints a YAML contract and runs schema and quality tests against a source with 'datacontract test', and ODCS has an SLA section. It could serve as a ready-made schema-drift check after each fetch, but that would mean a second descriptor format next to Frictionless; frictionless validate does the same job with the format already chosen.
projects.status: Amundsen and Vanna archive dates verified on their repo pages. Marquez: page lists 0.50.0 as recommended (changelog 2024-10-23), last commit date not visible. Evidence and Data Contract CLI: from search results only, primary pages not read.

results.angle_summary: Finance and macro systems confirm the bitemporal core of the spec and suggest five additions. (1) Copy FRED/ALFRED: validity interval per row (realtime_start, realtime_end), a "list vintages" call, and read modes "as of T", "first release only", "new and revised only". (2) Add named catalog snapshots (ArcticDB) so that an analysis pins all datasets at once. (3) Flag datasets whose knowledge time was not observed (backfilled history) instead of inventing fetched_at (vintage UNKNOWN_VINTAGE). (4) Stable ids of the form source/dataset, plus a "latest" alias (DBnomics, OWID). (5) Per-field metadata rules from OWID (unit, short_unit, description, expected update period, origin block). Challenges to the spec: FRED uses closed intervals, keep half-open but document it. Massive and OpenBB moved from one tool per endpoint to search + call + SQL, and Macrobond ships MCP and Skill together: the CLI + SKILL.md + SQL choice is consistent with the trend, MCP stays optional. No whole system is reusable.

projects.name: FRED / ALFRED API (St. Louis Fed)
projects.what: REST API for about 800k US macro series. ALFRED is the archive of vintages: every observation carries a real-time period that says when that value was the known one.
projects.overlap: Knowledge-time axis, as_of queries, revision policy, shape of the query API.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the docs pages. Each observation row has date, value, realtime_start, realtime_end (a validity interval on the knowledge axis, not just a fetched_at). Default real-time period is today, so a naive query returns the latest values ("FRED mode"). vintage_dates parameter gives the data as it existed on given dates. output_type has 4 modes: 1 by real-time period, 2 by vintage date all observations, 3 by vintage date new and revised only, 4 initial release only. A separate endpoint fred/series/vintagedates lists the dates on which a series changed (releases with no change are excluded). Ideas for Adele: (a) expose as_of, first_release and revisions_only as named query modes or DuckDB macros, (b) add `adele vintages <dataset>`, (c) store valid_from/valid_to on knowledge time for append-only datasets so that as_of is a simple range filter. Difference to note: FRED intervals are closed on both ends with sentinels 1776-07-04 and 9999-12-31, Adele uses half-open.
projects.status: Public service, active, free API key. Docs pages fetched 2026-11-13. Existence of an API v2 not checked.

projects.name: ArcticDB (Man Group)
projects.what: Serverless DataFrame database for Python: the client library reads and writes versioned, compressed dataframes directly on S3, Azure Blob or LMDB. Successor of Arctic.
projects.overlap: Versioned storage, as_of reads, snapshots across datasets, architecture without a query server.
projects.takeaways: Verified: Library.read(symbol, as_of=...) accepts an int (version number, negative counts back from latest), a str (snapshot name) or a datetime (data that existed at that time). library.snapshot(name) pins the current latest version of all symbols under one name, list_snapshots() and list_symbols(snapshot_name=...) inspect it. prune_previous_versions never deletes versions held by a snapshot. append creates a new version each time. Ideas for Adele: named snapshots of the whole catalog (e.g. a tag written at the start of a study) so that results are reproducible across a dozen datasets, and one as_of argument that accepts either a timestamp or a snapshot name. Not a candidate for storage: it replaces Parquet + DuckDB with its own format, and the licence is BSL 1.1 (production use needs a paid licence, each release converts to Apache 2.0 later, e.g. 6.21 on 2028-08-04).
projects.status: BSL 1.1, active (version 6.21 listed in the licence table). Exact latest release date not checked.

projects.name: Our World in Data ETL (owid/etl + owid-catalog)
projects.what: Pipeline that republishes hundreds of public datasets through fixed stages (snapshot, meadow, garden, grapher), with yaml metadata in git and a Python catalog library.
projects.overlap: Catalog descriptor (authored yaml + units per field), dataset ids, raw snapshots, provenance, expected refresh.
projects.takeaways: Verified: URIs are data://<channel>/<namespace>/<version>/<dataset> and snapshot://<namespace>/<version>/<file>, the version is the download date YYYY-MM-DD. Metadata reference has 4 levels (origin, dataset, table, indicator) with writing rules: indicator needs title, unit (plural, lower case), short_unit, description_short, description_processing, processing_level (minor or major), license. Origin needs producer, citation_full, date_published, date_accessed, url_main, url_download, license. Dataset has update_period_days (0 means no planned update). Ideas for Adele: keep the raw fetched file as an immutable snapshot next to the normalized Parquet, add an origin block and a description_processing field to the adele: extension, and adopt strict style rules for units so that agents get consistent text. The repo also contains owid_mcp and api_search folders plus AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (contents not read). OWID versions whole datasets by date, which fits yearly data and not 15-minute refreshes.
projects.status: MIT, about 17.9k commits on master, active. No tagged release shown. owid_mcp content and the catalog file formats not verified.

projects.name: DBnomics
projects.what: Free aggregator of public economic data (millions of series) with one fetcher per provider that runs daily, a common data model and one web API.
projects.overlap: Same architecture as the Adele server: scheduled fetchers, normalization, uniform ids, archive of revisions.
projects.takeaways: Verified: series id is provider/dataset/series_code (e.g. INSEE/IPC-2015/A.IPC...), the original provider codes are kept and values are never modified. Endpoints /providers/{p}, /datasets/{p}/{d}, /series/{p}/{d}/{s}?observations=1. Dataset codes can carry a release suffix (WEO:2019-10) and the reserved code "latest" resolves to the newest release with a 302 redirect. Every change from a provider is archived so that past revisions stay accessible. The docs are also published as /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt. Ideas for Adele: ids of the form source/dataset, keep source column codes in the descriptor next to normalized names, a "latest" alias for datasets with releases, and an llms.txt for the HTTP fallback. The API is not meant for bulk download (50 series by default), which the Parquet pull of Adele handles better.
projects.status: Public service, active (API v22). The repo dbnomics-data-model on git.nomics.world is archived and read-only (AGPLv3). Operator, data licence and storage backend not verified on the pages read.

projects.name: vintage (vintage-mcp)
projects.what: Small open-source Python library and MCP server that gives point-in-time access to about 18 free financial sources (SEC EDGAR, FRED/ALFRED, Treasury, ECB...) for agents and backtests.
projects.overlap: Closest analog of Adele in finance: bitemporal columns, as_of, few generic verbs for agents, local cache.
projects.takeaways: Verified on PyPI and the README: every value carries observed_at and known_at, and known_at is always kept as a column. as_of removes the rows that were published after the date. Sources that have no honest publication time are flagged UNKNOWN_VINTAGE instead of receiving an invented date. Six verbs (resolve, discover, fetch, events, backtest, benchmark) plus status, and "source is a parameter, never a separate tool", so new sources add no tools. Cache refresh depends on mutability: closed periods are never fetched again. Ideas for Adele: (a) a per-dataset flag that says whether knowledge time is observed or unknown for backfilled history (fetched_at of an initial bulk load is not the publication time, and an as_of query on it would be wrong), (b) in `adele pull`, skip delivery months that are older than the revision window of the dataset, (c) an `adele status` command.
projects.status: MIT, version 0.9.0 released 2026-08-07, 946 commits, 2 stars (single author, low adoption). Last commit date not checked.

projects.name: Massive.com MCP server (formerly Polygon.io)
projects.what: Official MCP server of a market data vendor. It replaced one tool per endpoint with three composable tools.
projects.overlap: Agent interface: discovery that is cheap in tokens, then SQL on fetched data.
projects.takeaways: Verified in the README: three tools only. search_endpoints (natural language search, detail levels "more" and "verbose"), call_api (any REST endpoint, store_as saves the result as a table), query_data (SQL on an in-memory SQLite, with SHOW TABLES and DESCRIBE). Limits by env vars (50 tables, 50000 rows by default). This is the same pattern as adele list --> describe --> query, which supports the choice of a small CLI with SQL over many specific commands. Ideas: graded detail in describe (short by default, a verbose flag for sample rows and full field notes) and default row limits on query output with a hint for the next page.
projects.status: MIT, install pinned to v0.10.0. Release date not checked.

projects.name: OpenBB Open Data Platform (ODP) and openbb-mcp-server
projects.what: Open-source toolset that integrates many data providers behind one Python, REST, CLI and MCP interface. Formerly OpenBB Platform.
projects.overlap: Uniform access layer over many sources, CLI, agent interface, skills.
projects.takeaways: Verified in the docs: the MCP server can hide all command tools behind 4 discovery tools (available_categories, available_tools, search_tools, call_tool) when enable_tool_discovery is set. Tool names derive from route paths (/api/v1/cboe/equity/quote --> cboe_equity_quote). It serves 5 bundled skills as skill://<name>/SKILL.md (among them use_openbb_cli and work_with_server), and adds a short system prompt that points the agent to the skills. So OpenBB ships skills through MCP, where Adele ships a skill without MCP. Ideas: deterministic names derived from the catalog path, and serving SKILL.md from the Adele server (HTTP endpoint) so that the skill version matches the server version. OpenBB is a pass-through to vendor APIs: it has no storage, no vintages and no freshness status, so it is not reusable for Adele.
projects.status: Apache 2.0, 6,886 commits on develop, active. Latest release version and date not verified (PyPI page did not load). Third-party pages disagree on the default of enable_tool_discovery, the docs page says False.

projects.name: Macrobond AI Data Feed
projects.what: Commercial macro data vendor that released on 2026-06-10 a service for AI workflows with three components: MCP, Skill and API.
projects.overlap: Delivery model for agents (Skill for coding agents, API underneath), point-in-time data.
projects.takeaways: Verified in the press release: MCP is positioned as the conversational interface for chat tools (Claude, ChatGPT), Skill as the programmatic interface for coding environments (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot), "distributed as a lightweight instruction layer", both on the same API. The service claims "revision-aware, point-in-time data for reproducible analysis" without technical detail. Relevance for Adele: an established vendor made the same split as the spec (skill + API for coding agents). MCP would only become useful if team members want access from chat clients that cannot run a CLI.
projects.status: Proprietary, licence required. Only the press release was read, no technical docs verified.

projects.name: Qlib point-in-time database (Microsoft)
projects.what: Data layer of the Qlib quant framework for fundamentals that get amended, so that a backtest sees the version known at each date.
projects.overlap: Bitemporal storage format for revisions.
projects.takeaways: Verified: one binary file per feature with 4 columns (date = publication date, period = reporting period, value, _next = byte offset of the next revision of the same period) plus an index file. Designed for quarterly or annual factors only, and the docs state that the computation "is not performed in the optimal way". Takeaway for Adele: this custom linked format is the opposite of what to do. Append-only Parquet rows with (delivery_start, fetched_at, value) and a DuckDB window query give the same result with standard tools. The naming (date vs period) also shows how easily the two time axes get confused, which supports explicit names such as delivery_start and known_at.
projects.status: MIT licence and maintenance activity not checked on this visit.

projects.name: EODHD MCP Server
projects.what: Official MCP server of the EODHD market data API.
projects.overlap: Agent interface (counter-example).
projects.takeaways: Verified: 88 MCP tools (85 read-only), one per API endpoint group, with transports streamable-http, sse and stdio, plus MCP prompts and resources. This is the design with one tool per endpoint that costs many tokens at connection time and that Massive and OpenBB moved away from. It is useful only as a contrast that supports the list/describe/query design of Adele. No bitemporal features seen.
projects.status: MIT, 178 commits. Release and last commit dates not shown on the page.

projects.name: Nasdaq Data Link (formerly Quandl)
projects.what: Commercial data marketplace with a time-series API (database_code/dataset_code ids) and a Tables API with a metadata endpoint.
projects.overlap: Uniform dataset ids, metadata endpoint per table.
projects.takeaways: Not verified on a primary page: the docs URLs now redirect (301) to https://data.nasdaq.com/accesstools, which returned 404 for the fetcher. From third-party pages only: the Tables API has a metadata call that returns column names, types, filterable columns and primary keys, and a refresh status. From memory, the VENDOR/CODE id and the per-table metadata call are the transferable ideas, and both are already in the Adele spec (describe).

projects.name: pandas-datareader
projects.what: Python library with one DataReader function over several remote sources (FRED, Stooq, World Bank...), which returns DataFrames.
projects.overlap: Uniform client over many sources.
projects.takeaways: From search results only: releases 0.11.0 and 0.11.1 in June 2026 restored compatibility with pandas 3, after a gap since 0.10.0 in July 2021. A GitHub issue reports that Stooq has required an API key since March 2026, which broke that reader. The library has no catalog, no metadata, no storage and no vintages. The lesson for Adele is negative: a thin client that calls upstream sources live breaks silently when a source changes. This supports fetching on the server with status alerts.

results.angle_summary: No project here replaces Adele as a whole. PUDL has the closest shape (Parquet + DuckDB + Frictionless datapackage + agent skill). ERDDAP and SDMX offer the best ideas on self-description. ERDDAP: the catalog is itself a queryable table (allDatasets) with minTime, maxTime, and a per-dataset staleness rule (testOutOfDate --> outOfDate index); units travel inside the data files; email/URL subscriptions. SDMX: structure (DSD) is separated from data, Eurostat publishes UPDATE_DATA and UPDATE_STRUCTURE timestamps separately, and the REST API defines updatedAfter, asOf and includeHistory (the same bitemporal semantics as Adele). Challenges to the spec: (1) add a catalog table that DuckDB can query, not only one descriptor per dataset; (2) define staleness as a declared rule, not a free-text "refresh" field; (3) OEMetadata already extends Frictionless with unit, resolution, timestamp alignment and aggregation type, so reuse its key names instead of inventing an "adele:" block from scratch; (4) the spec lacks alignment and aggregation type per field.

projects.name: PUDL (Public Utility Data Liberation, Catalyst Cooperative) + its agent skill
projects.what: Open pipeline that cleans US energy data (EIA, FERC, EPA) and publishes it as one Parquet file per table, plus a DuckDB file, with a Frictionless datapackage.json. A separate repo (https://github.com/catalyst-cooperative/agent-skills) holds an agent skill for it.
projects.overlap: Almost the whole Adele shape except the server side: Parquet as the primary format, DuckDB as the query engine, Frictionless descriptor as the catalog, an agent skill instead of MCP, versioned releases.
projects.takeaways: Verified on https://docs.catalyst.coop/pudl/en/nightly/data_access.html: (1) bucket prefixes nightly/ (ephemeral), stable/ (latest quarterly release), vYYYY.MM.N/ (archived); a simple model for Adele if a snapshot is ever needed. (2) A single pudl_parquet_datapackage.json describes the schema, types, constraints and foreign keys of every table without downloading data; that is the equivalent of 'adele describe'. (3) DuckDB reads the Parquet directly from S3; note their warning that a bucket name with dots needs URL_STYLE 'path'. (4) The agent skill 'pudl' helps an agent find tables, read column meanings and caveats on data quality, and load Parquet from S3 or a local folder, without the pudl Python package. The same repo ships a second skill 'datapackage' that teaches the Frictionless standard itself (install: npx skills add catalyst-cooperative/agent-skills -s pudl). Read both SKILL.md files before writing Adele's. Not verified: internal structure of the skill, and whether the data dictionary carries units as a structured field. PUDL has no 15-minute refresh, no knowledge-time axis, no API keys.
projects.status: Software MIT, data CC-BY-4.0. Nightly builds on weekdays, quarterly stable releases, Zenodo archive (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.3653158). SQLite output is deprecated and stops in 2027. Agent skills repo: MIT, 148 commits, labelled 'experimental'. Exact latest release date not checked.

projects.name: ERDDAP (NOAA)
projects.what: Java data server that gives a uniform URL-based way to download subsets of gridded and tabular (tabledap) scientific datasets in many file formats, with rich metadata per dataset. Used by NOAA, IOOS and many ocean institutes.
projects.overlap: Self-describing tabular server: catalog, units, time coverage, staleness, change notification, metadata-only responses, Parquet output.
projects.takeaways: Verified: (1) The catalog is itself a dataset, 'allDatasets', with one row per dataset and columns minTime, maxTime, timeSpacing, testOutOfDate, outOfDate, email, rss, summary (https://coastwatch.pfeg.noaa.gov/erddap/info/allDatasets/index.html). Adele could expose its catalog as a table that DuckDB can query, so the agent filters datasets with SQL. (2) Staleness is a declared rule: testOutOfDate (e.g. 'now-1day') compared with max(time); outOfDate is a numeric index (<1 up to date, >=1 out of date, >=2 very out of date). This is better than a free-text 'refresh: daily'. (3) Units travel with the data: .csv puts units on line 2, .csvp writes 'name (units)' in the header, .parquet stores names and units in the file metadata and .parquetWMeta stores more. Adele should write units and the descriptor into the Parquet key-value metadata, so a pulled file is self-describing. (4) Metadata-only responses (.das, .dds, .nccsvMetadata) are cheap for an agent. (5) Time: UTC assumed, ISO 8601, relative constraints such as time>now-7days and time>max(time)-10minutes; useful shortcuts for 'adele query'. (6) Subscriptions by email or by URL (webhook) and one RSS feed per dataset. ERDDAP's own doc admits that it 'is not very good at detecting changes to tabular datasets' because new rows do not change metadata: Adele must base alerts on fetch events and schema diffs, not on metadata diffs. Not reusable as a whole: Java servlet, no SQL, no knowledge-time axis, heavy datasets.xml configuration. reloadEveryNMinutes and updateEveryNMillis are seen only in forum threads, not verified in the docs.
projects.status: Active. Releases v2.30.0 (6 Apr 2026, adds Croissant manifest support, Parquet boolean fix), v2.31.0 (28 Aug), v2.31.1 (8 Sep; year assumed 2026, the page omits it). License: the GitHub page shows CC0-1.0 while the description says 'Apache and Apache-like'; not resolved. Community MCP servers exist (robertdcurrier/erddap2mcp, PyPI erddap-mcp 0.1.0); seen in search results only, the repo page returned 404.

projects.name: SDMX REST API (sdmx-twg/sdmx-rest)
projects.what: The official REST specification of SDMX, the standard used by Eurostat, ECB, OECD, BIS for statistical data and metadata exchange. Separates structure queries (dataflow, DSD, codelists, constraints) from data queries and availability queries.
projects.overlap: Bitemporal queries (as_of, revisions), incremental sync, and the separation between structural metadata and data.
projects.takeaways: Verified in doc/data.md: three parameters that match Adele's knowledge-time axis. updatedAfter: returns only what changed since the client's last query (added, revised and deleted observations); that is the semantics for 'adele pull'. asOf: 'Retrieve the data as they were at the specified point in time (aka time travel)'; same as Adele's as_of=. includeHistory: returns the current version plus all earlier ones, as successive datasets with action=Replace + validFromDate, or action=Delete + validToDate. Two points Adele's spec does not cover: deletions are explicit events (an append-only table with fetched_at cannot express 'this row was withdrawn' without a tombstone), and the spec says that updatedAfter later than asOf is a client error. Verified in doc/availability.md: the availability query returns an AvailabilityConstraint with the distinct values per dimension, optional time range (validFrom/validTo) and optional obsCount and seriesCount; i.e. server-computed coverage, separate from authored structure, as Adele plans. Time filter syntax: c[TIME_PERIOD]=ge:2020-01+le:2020-12. Do not adopt SDMX formats (XML, cube model with codelists): too heavy for a dozen flat tables.
projects.status: Open specification on GitHub, current docs list SDMX-JSON 2.1.0, SDMX-ML 3.1.0, SDMX-CSV 2.1.0. License and last commit date not checked.

projects.name: Eurostat dissemination API (SDMX 3.0 + Catalogue API)
projects.what: Eurostat's public implementation of SDMX 2.1 and 3.0, plus a catalogue API (table of contents, RSS of updates).
projects.overlap: Server-computed fields in the catalog entry: coverage, row count, last update of data versus last update of structure.
projects.takeaways: Verified: each dataflow carries five annotations. OBS_COUNT (e.g. 95814), OBS_PERIOD_OVERALL_OLDEST (2002), OBS_PERIOD_OVERALL_LATEST (2014), UPDATE_STRUCTURE (2021-02-08T23:00:00+0100, last change of dimensions or of their positions), UPDATE_DATA (2023-05-10T11:00:00+0200). The key idea for Adele: two separate timestamps, data_updated_at and schema_updated_at, in the server-computed block. An agent that cached a describe output can compare schema_updated_at alone to know whether its cache is still valid. Per the search result on the RSS guide (not fetched), the catalogue RSS emits distinct events for a data-only update, a structure-only update, or both, over the last 7 days; the same three-way split fits Adele's email alerts. Formats: SDMX-ML, SDMX-CSV 2.0, TSV, JSON-stat; no Parquet. This page documents no incremental parameter (non-versioned artefacts 'need to be requested again for updates'). Eurostat gives no ETA of next refresh in these annotations.
projects.status: Live public service, pages fetched 2026-11. Units are an attribute or dimension in the DSD (per the structure query guide), not a property of a column.

projects.name: OEMetadata (Open Energy Platform)
projects.what: A metadata standard for energy data, as nested JSON, based on the Frictionless Data Package specification and the FAIR principles. Used by the German Open Energy Platform.
projects.overlap: Exactly the 'adele:' extension block: Frictionless plus energy-specific keys for units and time series.
projects.takeaways: Verified in metadata_key_description.md (version OEMetadata-2.0): temporal.timeseries[] has start, end, resolutionValue, resolutionUnit, alignment (timestamp at the left, right or centre of the interval) and aggregationType (sum, average or current value). Each field has name, type, unit (or null), nullable, isAbout (ontology terms), valueReference. Sources and licenses carry attribution and copyrightStatement. Top-level publicationDate, embargoPeriod. Each key has a badge level (Iron, Bronze, Silver...) that states how complete a descriptor is. Recommendation: reuse these key names inside Adele's descriptor (unit per field, resolutionValue/Unit, alignment, aggregationType) instead of inventing new ones. Adele's spec fixes alignment globally (half-open intervals, so left) but says nothing on aggregationType; for electricity it matters whether a 15-minute value is mean power (MW) or energy (MWh), and a unit alone does not always settle it. OEMetadata has no key for update frequency, freshness, status or revision policy: Adele's block is still needed for those. A JSON schema, template and example are in the 'latest' folder; a PyPI package exists (badge seen).
projects.status: Code MIT, schema and examples CC0. Version 2.0 seen; Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15019562. Release date and recent commit activity not checked.

projects.name: Our World in Data ETL + owid-catalog
projects.what: The compute graph that builds all OWID datasets, with metadata authored in YAML next to each step, and a Python client (owid.catalog) to search and fetch tables, indicators and charts.
projects.overlap: Authored YAML metadata in git + computed catalog; Python client with search/fetch; exposure to LLM agents.
projects.takeaways: Verified in the metadata reference: variable.unit and variable.short_unit are both required for every indicator; variable.processing_level (minor/major); variable.description_key (bullets of key facts, good material for an agent); origin.date_published, origin.date_accessed, origin.version_producer, origin.license; dataset.update_period_days ('Expected number of days between consecutive updates', required integer, 0 if no update planned). Adele's 'refresh' can be as simple as that plus an expected lag. Client (https://docs.owid.io/projects/etl/libraries/catalog/api/): client.tables.search(), client.tables.fetch('channel/namespace/version/dataset/table'), and fetch(load_data=False) to get structure and metadata without rows (same as adele describe); the catalog index is cached locally with refresh_index=True to force. The repo contains CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and an owid_mcp directory: an MCP server (fastMCP) with search_indicator, run_sql (read-only SQL on a public Datasette), fetch_indicator_metadata. Its README states that enabling it adds about 7k tokens to the initial context; this figure supports Adele's choice of a skill + CLI over MCP. OWID versions a dataset by a date in its path; it has no knowledge-time axis inside a table and no sub-daily refresh.
projects.status: MIT. About 17,900 commits, nightly full rebuild on Buildkite. No tagged releases. Last commit date not checked.

projects.name: STAC (Collection spec + table extension)
projects.what: SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog: a JSON specification for catalogs of geospatial assets, with a companion API. The 'table' extension (https://github.com/stac-extensions/table) describes tabular assets.
projects.overlap: Catalog + API pattern; temporal extent; description of columns for Parquet assets.
projects.takeaways: Verified: Collection.extent.temporal.interval is a list of [start, end] RFC 3339 UTC timestamps where null means open-ended (Adele can use end=null or a 'live' flag for running datasets). The spec text does not say whether the interval is closed or half-open, which is the kind of ambiguity Adele wants to avoid: state it in every descriptor. 'summaries' gives per-field ranges or distinct value sets (useful for bidding_zone: list the distinct zones in the descriptor). item_assets describes the files without listing them. Table extension: table:columns (name, description, type), table:row_count, table:primary_datetime (names the main time column; Adele could name delivery_start this way). It defines no unit field (it only allows extra properties) and its maturity is 'Pilot'. STAC's Item-per-file model maps onto Adele's monthly partitions (one Item per partition with its own datetime range and checksum), which would give 'adele pull' a manifest to diff; but full STAC is geospatial and oversized for Adele.
projects.status: STAC spec: stable, widely used; current version number not shown on the fetched page. Table extension: Apache-2.0, schema v1.3.0, maturity Pilot.

projects.name: Croissant (MLCommons)
projects.what: A metadata format for ML datasets, JSON-LD built on schema.org, describing files (FileObject/FileSet) and RecordSets with typed fields.
projects.overlap: Alternative to Frictionless as the descriptor format; handling of datasets that keep changing.
projects.takeaways: Verified (Croissant 1.0, 2024-03-01): isLiveDataset is an optional boolean for datasets whose data changes over time; the spec advises no checksums on files that still change, and to bump the version only for structural or backward-incompatible changes. That rule fits Adele: descriptor version = schema version, not data version. RecordSets support 'examples' (like Adele's 5 sample rows) and 'key'. The spec has no unit property and no temporal coverage, so it is weaker than Frictionless + OEMetadata for Adele. Its relevance: ERDDAP added Croissant manifest output in v2.30.0 (April 2026), so it is becoming the interchange format toward ML tools. An export 'adele describe --format croissant' is a cheap option for later, not a base.
projects.status: Version 1.0 fetched; newer versions not checked. License not checked.

projects.name: CKAN DataStore API (also the base of opendata.swiss)
projects.what: The tabular storage extension of the CKAN open data portal: loads resources into PostgreSQL and exposes search, SQL and schema endpoints.
projects.overlap: HTTP fallback API: query endpoint with SQL, info endpoint, data dictionary.
projects.takeaways: Verified: datastore_search (filters, limit default 100, max 32000), datastore_search_sql (one PostgreSQL SELECT, disabled by default, enforced timeout, 32000 rows cap, response flag records_truncated), datastore_info (row count, sizes, native types, nullability). Lessons for Adele's HTTP fallback: enforce a row cap and a timeout, and return an explicit 'truncated' flag so the agent knows the answer is partial; recommend keyset pagination over offset. The data dictionary has label, notes (description), type_override per field, and no built-in unit. Gotcha documented by CKAN: uppercase column names need double quotes in SQL, otherwise null results; Adele should normalize every column to lower snake_case. CKAN itself is far too heavy for one box with a dozen datasets.
projects.status: Docs 'latest' mention features of CKAN 2.12. License and release date not checked.

projects.name: DCAT-AP CH (opendata.swiss) / DCAT-AP (data.europa.eu)
projects.what: The RDF metadata profile that Swiss and European open data portals require for dataset and distribution descriptions.
projects.overlap: Dataset-level catalog fields: update cadence, temporal coverage, modification dates.
projects.takeaways: Verified: dct:accrualPeriodicity takes a URI of the EU frequency vocabulary (e.g. .../frequency/ANNUAL); dct:temporal is a period with startDate and endDate, both required (omit it if the end is unknown, so a running dataset has no coverage at all); dct:modified, dct:issued. There is no column-level schema and no units: only dct:conformsTo or free text. Conclusion: DCAT describes 'what exists and how often it is updated' at a coarse level and cannot answer an agent's questions about fields. The only reusable element is the EU frequency vocabulary as a controlled list for cadence, and ISO 8601 durations (already in Adele's spec) are more precise. data.europa.eu was not fetched.
projects.status: Live. Exact DCAT-AP CH version not stated on the page (links to 2.0; an example file is named v3). CKAN as the platform of opendata.swiss is inferred from URIs, not stated.

projects.name: Open Power System Data (time series package)
projects.what: A Frictionless data package of European load, generation and price time series (mostly from ENTSO-E) at 15, 30 and 60 minute resolution, in CSV, XLSX and SQLite.
projects.overlap: Same data domain and same descriptor format (datapackage.json) as Adele.
projects.takeaways: Verified: one file per resolution (15, 30, 60 min); utc_timestamp is the start of the period, with a second column cet_cest_timestamp; units are only in field descriptions (MW; EUR for prices but GBP for Great Britain). Two lessons: (1) a unit can vary by row (currency per bidding zone), so Adele needs either a unit column or one field per unit, and a single 'unit per field' in the descriptor is not always enough for prices; (2) their wide layout (one column per country and variable) forces the remark that missing fields are to be expected; Adele's long grain (bidding_zone, delivery_start) avoids that. The package is a static snapshot, so it does not address freshness or revisions.
projects.status: Stale: latest version 2020-10-06, data until mid-2020. Not a live source. License not checked.

projects.name: Socrata SODA API
projects.what: The query API of the Socrata (Tyler) open data platform used by many US governments, with a SQL-like language (SoQL).
projects.overlap: HTTP query API with a SQL dialect and application tokens.
projects.takeaways: Verified: SODA 3.0 moves endpoints to /api/v3/views/ID/query.json, requires a user login or an application token on every query, separates /query (machine-readable) from /export (human-readable formats), and prefers POST for queries. projects.name: TimeDB and EnergyDB (rebase-energy)
projects.what: TimeDB is a small Python client for '3-dimensional' time series on ClickHouse, built by an energy forecasting company. EnergyDB (https://github.com/rebase-energy/energydb) adds an asset hierarchy, a series catalog in PostgreSQL and units.
projects.overlap: Adele's time model: delivery time versus knowledge time, revisions, as_of queries, units per series.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the READMEs: TimeDB uses three time axes, not two: valid_time (the time that the value describes), knowledge_time (when the value was predicted or known) and change_time (when the row was written or corrected). Corrections are new rows with a newer change_time, never overwrites; reads return the latest state by default, include_knowledge_time=True returns the full history, and read_relative() gives per-window cutoffs for backtests. Rows carry changed_by and annotation. skip_unchanged=True drops identical rows before insert. EnergyDB declares a canonical unit per series and converts with pint. Challenge to the Adele spec: for forecast datasets (day-ahead load or wind forecasts), 'fetched_at' is not the same thing as the publication time of the forecast. Adele should decide whether knowledge time means 'published by the source' or 'fetched by Adele' and may need both columns. Also copy skip_unchanged for append-only datasets, otherwise a fetch every 15 minutes multiplies identical rows. Storage (ClickHouse + PostgreSQL) does not fit Adele's Parquet + DuckDB choice.

results.angle_summary: No project found combines Adele's parts (scheduled fetchers + Frictionless catalog + bitemporal Parquet + CLI/skill) for European power data; existing open-source work is API clients, MCP proxies (Luminus) and toy pipelines. The closest prior art is Catalyst Cooperative's agent-skills (generic Frictionless datapackage skill + PUDL skill on Parquet/DuckDB): if Adele descriptors stay valid Frictionless, that skill and the official duckdb-skills work unchanged, so the Adele skill can be thin. Agnes (Keboola; repo returned 404, unverified) reportedly implements the same pull design (manifest --> MD5 --> changed files, pull at session start). Two challenges to the spec: (1) TimeDB separates knowledge_time from change_time; for forecast datasets, Adele's fetched_at mixes "published by source" with "fetched by Adele", and unchanged rows should be skipped on append. (2) A frozen DuckLake over HTTPS could replace the custom partition sync and give snapshot time travel. llms.txt alone carries no dataset metadata (gridstatus).

Every source agrees on one point: filtering SQL text fails (Arc CVE-2026-47735, the Quack docs warning on WITH ... INSERT), and DuckDB read-only mode alone still lets a query read local files (MotherDuck README, Redash CVE-2026-77371). The controls must be set in the engine. Minimal set for one box and ten trusted users: (1) parquet reached only through allowed_directories, then enable_external_access=false, autoinstall/autoload off, community extensions off, threads/memory_limit/max_temp_directory_size, lock_configuration=true last; (2) a timer that calls interrupt() (DuckDB has no native timeout); (3) cap on rows and bytes; (4) unprivileged user or container; (5) one hashed key per person, TLS and rate limit in the reverse proxy; (6) a log line per query (key id, SQL, duration, rows). Challenge to the spec: `adele pull` plus local DuckDB removes most of this attack surface, so remote `query` could be secondary. DuckDB 2.0 Quack may replace a custom HTTP endpoint.

projects.name: DuckDB docs: Securing DuckDB (v2.0)
projects.what: Official DuckDB guide on running SQL that is not fully trusted. It lists the engine settings that restrict files, network, extensions, secrets and resources.
projects.overlap: Server query engine: configuration of the DuckDB connection behind `adele query` and the HTTP API.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the page: SET enable_external_access=false; SET allowed_directories=[...]; allowed_paths; SET disabled_filesystems='LocalFileSystem'; SET lock_configuration=true; SET allowed_configs=['memory_limit','threads'] (keeps some settings adjustable after the lock); SET threads; SET memory_limit; SET max_temp_directory_size; autoload_known_extensions=false; autoinstall_known_extensions=false; allow_community_extensions=false; allow_persistent_secrets=false. The page states "Treat SQL in DuckDB like code in Bash or Python", says the settings are defense in depth and "not a substitute for proper sandboxing", advises never to run as root, and suggests a container with restricted capabilities. It documents no native query timeout: "Implement strict query timeouts at the application level." For Adele: allow only the parquet root in allowed_directories, disable external access, set the lock last. Since the docs are now at 2.0, re-check setting names against the DuckDB version that Adele pins.
projects.status: Official docs, current (URL path is /docs/2.0/, the /stable/ URL redirects there). Fetched and verified 2026-11-13.

projects.name: DuckDB Quack extension (remote protocol of DuckDB)
projects.what: DuckDB extension that turns a DuckDB instance into an HTTP server to which other DuckDB clients ATTACH with 'quack:host' URIs (default port 9494). It was not in the list of starting points.
projects.overlap: The server endpoint that accepts arbitrary SQL, key issuance per team member, the client (a local DuckDB can ATTACH the remote one).
projects.takeaways: Verified on the security and overview pages: binds to localhost by default (allow_other_hostname=true needed otherwise); the docs advise a reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy) for TLS and say not to expose it directly. Authentication runs once per connection and authorization runs before each query, both as SQL callbacks: SET GLOBAL quack_authentication_function='check_token' with a quack_tokens table gives one token per user, and rotation is a row update. SET GLOBAL quack_authorization_function='read_only'. The docs warn that a prefix regex is not a robust read-only filter ("a query starting with WITH can still contain an INSERT") and recommend attaching the database read-only or checking the parsed statement type. No limits or timeouts are documented. For Adele: a candidate to replace a custom HTTP query endpoint, but the engine settings from the Securing guide and a timeout are still needed.
projects.status: Official DuckDB docs under /docs/2.0/ and /docs/1.5/. Stability status (experimental or stable), license and whether it is a core extension: not stated on the pages that I fetched, not checked further.

projects.name: simonw/research: duckdb-security
projects.what: Research report by Simon Willison (January 2026) with demo scripts that test DuckDB settings for untrusted queries from Python, including a timeout.
projects.overlap: Server query engine in Python: exact recipe for a restricted connection and for query timeouts.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the README: duckdb.connect(path, read_only=True); config enable_external_access=false blocks read_csv, read_parquet, COPY TO/FROM and ATTACH; allowed_directories and allowed_paths keep working after external access is disabled; SET lock_configuration=true must come last, and it also blocks USE (known issue). Timeout recipe: threading.Timer(timeout_sec, con.interrupt), catch duckdb.InterruptException. Resource limits: threads, memory_limit, max_temp_directory_size. Caveats: the report says it is AI-generated, shows no test output and does not name the DuckDB version, and it does not test INSTALL/LOAD. Adele should turn these demos into its own test suite (each hostile statement must fail) and run it at every DuckDB upgrade.
projects.status: Blog post dated 2026-01-16 (https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jan/16/duckdb-security/). License of the repo not checked.

projects.name: Arc (Basekick-Labs), CVE-2026-47735
projects.what: Time-series database built on DuckDB and Parquet with an authenticated HTTP SQL endpoint. An advisory showed that its regex filter on SQL let any authenticated user read local files.
projects.overlap: Incident report for exactly Adele's design: API key + HTTP + arbitrary DuckDB SQL over parquet.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the advisory: the validator blocked only read_parquet( and one more function by regex; read_csv, read_csv_auto, read_json, glob, parquet_metadata were not blocked. Impact: reading auth.db (hashes of API tokens), the config file with S3 secrets and TLS keys, /proc/self/environ, and requests to cloud metadata addresses when httpfs is loaded. Fix in 2026.06.1: SET GLOBAL allowed_directories to the legitimate paths, then SET GLOBAL enable_external_access=false, then read the flag back to check it. After that DuckDB refuses INSTALL/LOAD, but extensions that are already loaded stay callable. For Adele: never filter SQL text; do not load httpfs in the query process; keep the key store and the config outside allowed_directories; verify the settings after setting them.
projects.status: Advisory GHSA-p2j4-c4g6-rpf5, fixed in 2026.06.1. Product repo https://github.com/Basekick-Labs/arc not fetched; license not checked.

projects.what: Redash (BI tool) added a DuckDB data source that left enable_external_access at its default. Users with query access could read and write files of the server process.
projects.overlap: Second incident for the same threat: authenticated user + arbitrary DuckDB SQL.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the CVE page: versions 26.0.0 to before 26.9.0; CVSS 4.0 score 9.3 (critical); low-privilege users could use native file-reading functions and COPY TO with the privileges of the Redash process, and read REDASH_COOKIE_SECRET, which allows forged sessions. Fixed in 26.9.0. Lesson for Adele: the default DuckDB connection is unsafe for any remote SQL, even from trusted team members, because their agents can be steered by injected text. The secret that signs or stores API keys must not be readable by the query process (separate user or separate process).
projects.status: CVE published 2026, fixed in Redash 26.9.0. Verified on OpenCVE only; the Redash advisory itself was not fetched.

projects.name: caddy-duckdb-module (tobilg)
projects.what: Caddy web server module that exposes DuckDB over REST with API keys, roles, and limits.
projects.overlap: HTTP API with an API key per team member, limits on results, timeouts. Shows a complete small design on one box.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the README: access_mode read_only or read_write (default read_write); API keys stored as bcrypt hashes in a separate auth database, each key bound to a role (admin, editor, reader; custom roles per table with operations c/r/u/d/q), optional expiry per key; the auth tables cannot be queried through the API; query_timeout default 10s; max_rows_per_page 100; absolute_max_rows 10000; threads 4; memory_limit. Rate limiting is "intentionally not implemented" and delegated to a Caddy plugin (caddy-rate-limit). Each request gets an X-Request-ID that appears in logs. For Adele: same split is sensible (Caddy does TLS and rate limit, the application does keys, timeout, caps); key table with hash, owner, created, expires gives issuance and rotation for ten people without more machinery.
projects.status: MIT, 81 stars, only 4 commits shown, no releases. Small project, reuse as a whole would be risky. Last commit date not checked.

projects.name: GizmoSQL and its successor Hardcharger (GizmoData)
projects.what: GizmoSQL is an Arrow Flight SQL server in front of DuckDB. Its README now says it is in maintenance mode and recommends Hardcharger, a new server for DuckDB 2.0 by the same company.
projects.overlap: Remote SQL endpoint with authentication, timeout, audit; an alternative to building Adele's query server.
projects.takeaways: GizmoSQL, verified on the README: Apache-2.0 core; TLS/mTLS, JWT tokens and --query-timeout (default 0 = unlimited) are in the core; kill session, per-catalog permissions, SSO, session instrumentation are Enterprise only; --print-queries logs queries; INIT_SQL_COMMANDS env variable is the place for DuckDB hardening settings; single username/password by default. No read-only flag seen on the page. Hardcharger, from one HackerNoon article by the vendor (announced 2026-10-21): Apache 2.0, no editions, SQL over HTTP/1.1 with Arrow IPC, bearer tokens, roles and grants down to columns checked against the query plan, KILL SESSION, statement queue and timeouts, "tamper-evident audit log", refusal of credential and system files at the filesystem layer of DuckDB. This is far more than ten trusted users need, and it is three weeks old.
projects.status: GizmoSQL: Apache-2.0 core, maintenance mode (stated on README), bundles DuckDB 1.5.6 / 2.0.0 edge. Hardcharger: claims from a vendor article only (https://hackernoon.com/what-the-heck-is-hardcharger), repo URL not found, not verified.

projects.name: DuckDB MCP extension (duckdb_mcp) security guide
projects.what: Community DuckDB extension that makes DuckDB an MCP server or client. Its security guide lists per-statement-class switches and exposure defaults.
projects.overlap: Agent-facing endpoint: which statement classes to allow, timeouts, authentication, and the alternative of narrow parameterized tools.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the guide: the execute tool is disabled by default; execute_allow_load, execute_allow_attach and execute_allow_set default to false (LOAD, ATTACH, SET are the three statement classes to deny even to trusted clients); query_timeout_ms (example 30000); auth_token with require_auth; bind to 127.0.0.1 and put a reverse proxy in front "for TLS, authentication, rate limiting, and logging"; run in a container as non-root; start with -readonly or ATTACH (READ_ONLY). It recommends publishing narrow parameterized tools with capped results (LIMIT LEAST($limit, 100)) instead of the general query tool. For Adele: the same idea supports a few fixed, parameterized fetch commands in the CLI next to free SQL.
projects.status: Community extension, documentation on Read the Docs (latest). License, repo activity and release: not checked.

projects.name: httpserver DuckDB community extension (Query.farm, formerly quackscience)
projects.what: Community extension that exposes a running DuckDB process over HTTP: POST a SQL string, get JSON back.
projects.overlap: HTTP API fallback for `adele query`.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the extension page and repo: started with SELECT httpserve_start('0.0.0.0', 9999, 'user:pass'); authentication is one shared secret, either HTTP basic or an X-API-Key header, and an empty string disables it; no read-only mode, TLS, timeouts or limits are described; logs via DUCKDB_HTTPSERVER_DEBUG or DUCKDB_HTTPSERVER_SYSLOG. One shared key means no per-user revocation and no attribution in an audit log, which fails Adele's requirement of a key per team member. All hardening would have to come from the DuckDB settings and a proxy. Quack now covers the same need with per-user tokens.
projects.status: MIT, 285 stars, repo moved to https://github.com/Query-farm/httpserver (v2.0 branch, 110 commits). Compatibility matrix lists DuckDB 1.4.4 to 2.0.0. Release date not shown.

projects.name: Supabase MCP "lethal trifecta" incident (write-up by Simon Willison)
projects.what: July 2025 demonstration by General Analysis: text in a support ticket made a Cursor agent with the Supabase MCP read a private table and write its content where the attacker could see it.
projects.overlap: Threat model of agents that run SQL: what read-only does and does not protect.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the post: the attack needs three things together (access to private data, exposure to hostile instructions, a channel to send data out). Read-only removes the write channel inside the database, but Willison says the risk stays large. Applied to Adele (my reasoning, not from the post): the datasets are public, so the private data at risk are the files and keys on the server and on the laptop of the team member; hostile instructions could arrive in free-text fields of upstream sources (for example outage or remark fields from ENTSO-E) that `describe` sample rows or query results place in the agent's context. Controls: server process that cannot read anything but parquet, no httpfs in the query process (no outbound channel), and a note in SKILL.md that cell values are data, never instructions. A Snyk audit of a public DuckDB CLI skill (https://skills.sh/ysm-dev/skills/duckdb-cli/security/snyk, verified) flags exactly this: a skill that teaches reading remote http/S3 files gets a prompt-injection warning.
projects.status: Blog post of 2025-07-06, fetched. The original General Analysis report was not fetched.

projects.name: ROAPI
projects.what: Rust server that creates read-only REST, GraphQL and SQL APIs over static files (parquet, csv, etc.) with Apache DataFusion as engine.
projects.overlap: Read-only query endpoint over parquet, as an alternative engine to DuckDB.
projects.takeaways: Verified on the README: "automatically spins up read-only APIs for static datasets"; engine is Arrow + DataFusion; an "authentication layer" appears only as an item of a feature checklist with no description; no query timeout, row cap or rate limit is documented. The useful idea is that an engine with no write path and no file functions reachable from SQL needs fewer controls than DuckDB. But Adele's clients use DuckDB SQL locally after `pull`, and two SQL dialects (remote and local) would confuse the agent.
